Rolex · ref. 226570

Explorer II

Tool watch / GMT · 39–42mm · 100m · automatic · 1971–2026

The Explorer II is a robust tool watch originally designed for speleologists to distinguish day from night in dark environments. It is defined by its fixed 24-hour engraved bezel and a distinct, brightly colored 24-hour hand.

The story

Introduced in 1971 with reference 1655, the Explorer II was created for cave explorers. Initially, its 24-hour hand was linked to the main hour hand for day/night indication. A major turning point came in 1985 with the reference 16550, which introduced an independently adjustable 24-hour hand, transforming it into a GMT watch capable of tracking a second time zone. This reference also introduced the option of a white "Polar" dial. Subsequent generations saw refinements in movements, materials, and an increase in case size from 39mm to 40mm, and eventually to 42mm with the reference 216570 in 2011, which also brought back the iconic orange 24-hour hand from the original model. The latest reference, 226570, was released in 2021 for the model's 50th anniversary, featuring an updated caliber.

References by era

16551971–1984
The original Explorer II, nicknamed 'Freccione.' It featured a 39mm case and a prominent orange 24-hour hand.
165501985–1989
A transitional reference that introduced a 40mm case, sapphire crystal, and an independent GMT hand. This was the first reference to offer a white 'Polar' dial.
165701989–2011
A long-running reference with a 40mm case. Early models used tritium for luminescence, later switching to Luminova and Super-LumiNova. It housed both the Caliber 3185 and later the 3186.
2165702011–2021
Released for the 40th anniversary, this reference increased the case size to 42mm and reintroduced the large orange 24-hour hand as a tribute to the original ref. 1655.
2265702021–present
The current model, launched for the 50th anniversary. It maintains the 42mm case size but features a new generation movement and subtly refined lugs and bracelet.
